# `Q-25-9` — Component module could not be prepared

> A component's TypeScript or JSX module, or one it imports, failed to transpile, could not be read, or has an import that names no file. The component was not shipped; its element keeps the static content.

## What this means

A `.tsx`, `.ts` or `.jsx` component is turned into browser JavaScript
while the page renders: types are stripped, JSX is compiled, and every
relative import inside the project is shipped beside it (TypeScript files
transpiled, plain JavaScript copied). This warning means one step of that
failed. The message names the file and, for a syntax error, the line and
column inside it. When the entry module fails, the component is left out
of the page; when an imported helper fails, the entry still ships and the
browser reports the missing module.

## Why this happens

- A syntax or type-syntax error in the module. The position in the message
  is in the module, not in the document that declares it.
- An import such as `./util.ts` or `./util.js` that names no file (the
  `.js`-for-`.ts` convention is accepted: `./util.js` finds `util.ts`).
- The file is unreadable.

## How to fix

Fix the module at the position given, or the import that names no file,
and render again. Bare imports (`react`, a package name) are not resolved
here: `react` comes from the page's import map, and other packages are not
supported yet (Q-25-3).

## Related

- The components guide (`docs/guides/authoring/components.qmd`) describes
  the `components:` key, the element contract and the runtime.
